s1.syndrome_frame: Severe, persistent, unilateral facial pain with trigeminal nerve involvement and abnormal sensations
salient_findings: Persistent severe pain on the left side of the face
Pain localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
Allodynia to cold air and hypersensitivity to touch in the affected area
key_facts: 36-year-old woman
Received third dose of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine
Pain started the day after vaccination
Pain initially affected the entire left hemiface
Pain localized to V2 and V3 distributions within days
Attacks last 4-5 seconds
Attacks triggered by jaw movement during eating or tooth brushing
Pain reaches 10/10 on a numeric pain scale
Distorted sensations in the V2 region during attacks
Sensory testing otherwise normal
No other neurological deficits
No relevant past medical or family history
Routine laboratory tests normal
RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and other infections negative
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head shows no abnormalities

differentials: Short-Lasting Unilateral Neuralgiform Headache with Conjunctival Injection and Tearing
per_call: Short-Lasting Unilateral Neuralgiform Headache with Conjunctival Injection and Tearing

shortlist.label: Trigeminal Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Classic presentation of severe, unilateral facial pain with trigeminal nerve involvement and abnormal sensations

shortlist.label: Trigeminal Neuroma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of trigeminal nerve dysfunction and facial pain

shortlist.label: SUNCT Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Short-lasting, unilateral neuralgiform headache with conjunctival injection and tearing, similar to patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Trigeminal Neuropathic Pain
shortlist.why_kept: Pain characteristics and trigeminal nerve involvement are consistent with neuropathic pain

shortlist.label: Postherpetic Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Although no clear history of herpes zoster, the pain characteristics and distribution are plausible for postherpetic neuralgia

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, are characteristic of Trigeminal Neuralgia.

rejected.label: Trigeminal Neuroma
rejected.why: There is no evidence of a tumor on the contrast-enhanced MRI of the head

rejected.label: SUNCT Syndrome
rejected.why: SUNCT Syndrome typically involves more frequent and shorter-lasting attacks, often with conjunctival injection and lacrimation, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Trigeminal Neuropathic Pain
rejected.why: While the patient has neuropathic pain, the specific distribution and triggers are more consistent with Trigeminal Neuralgia

rejected.label: Postherpetic Neuralgia
rejected.why: There is no history of herpes zoster infection, which is typically required for a diagnosis of Postherpetic Neuralgia
